batch: Correct and classify three works from official journal, institutional and publisher evidence
policy: These are work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities or authenticity, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: The complete official article publishes a detailed cultural, chronological and inscriptional study of one fourteenth-century Arabic metal bowl; it is adjacent scholarship and not an in-scope late-antique Aramaic bowl.
The publisher describes a sustained study of law and magic in rabbinic literature and Babylonian incantation bowls rather than an edition of a numbered object corpus.
The institutional abstract frames the article as a social and professional study of bowl producers and their scribal context, not an object edition.

The publisher-hosted first-page abstract states that this Jewish Babylonian Aramaic bowl is published for the first time and identifies its client, protective purpose and Hebrew citation of Isaiah 40:6-8.
